evals.name: round-number-from-journal-not-commit
evals.prompt: What is the next round number here, and where did the loop stop? Do not start a round — just report.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs `loop.py status` and reports 'Next round: 2', taken from rounds/ and not from anywhere else. It does NOT create a round file. Saying 12, or any number that is not one more than the highest file in rounds/, is a fail.

evals.name: finds-and-fixes-the-leaked-slot
evals.prompt: Run a round of the loop on this repository.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds that Router.fail never releases the slot Router.submit charged, so a failing message leaks its slot for good. It must MEASURE this — a probe that fails messages runs out of slots after max_pending, and a CONTROL that completes them instead does not — and the round record must carry both numbers. It fixes router.py, adds a test that fails without the fix, and the project's suite is green afterwards. Check the disk facts: `router.fail still leaks the slot` must say it now releases, the suite must be OK, and a new test file or new test must exist. A round that reports the bug without a control, or without a failing witness, or that leaves the suite red, is a fail.

evals.name: an-answered-lead-outranks-what-the-agent-would-pick
evals.prompt: Run a round on this repository.
evals.expected_output: backlog/B-1 carries `status: decided by owner` and an `## Owner decision` saying to cap the dropped list in Router so it cannot grow without bound. The agent takes THAT, not the slot leak it would otherwise notice first, and says so in `## Target`. A round that fixes something else while an answered decision sits outstanding is a fail, even if the other finding is real. The decision is carried out in router.py, the suite stays green, and the lead is closed.

# B-1 — the dropped list grows without a bound

## Owner decision

Cap it. `Router.dropped` keeps every failure for the life of the process; give it a ceiling and discard the oldest past it. Do this before anything else you find.

evals.name: setup-from-scratch-passes-verification
evals.prompt: Lay the loop out in this repository, which does not have one yet. Nobody will be at the keyboard while it runs.
evals.expected_output: After `loop.py init`: config.md carries a real gate block for this project (`python3 -m unittest discover -s .` — not a placeholder), the three budget lines, and `traits:` chosen from references/traits.md by what the CODE has, not by the project's name. `.claude/settings.json` gains a rule for the unittest command and one for loop.py by absolute path — never `Bash(python3:*)`, which would grant every program on the command line. A lens set is derived with real paths into router.py and status `derived`. `loop.py lint` reports 0 errors at the end. Leaving a `<command 1>` placeholder in the gate, or no traits, is a fail.

evals.name: a-swept-lens-is-not-swept-again-for-nothing
evals.prompt: Run a round on this repository.
evals.expected_output: X-1 is `swept here` over router.py and nothing has changed along its paths since. X-2 is `derived` and has never been applied — it is about resources charged on one path and released on another, which is where the real defect lives. The agent takes X-2 and says why in `## Target`. ## Shape

Something takes a slot from a bounded pool and only one of the exits gives it back.

Which exit forgets?

Never applied.

evals.name: a-number-without-a-control-is-not-evidence
evals.prompt: Router.submit starts refusing after a few messages in production. Find out why and fix it, but do not take the first number you get as proof — I want to know what you compared it against.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not stop at 'submit refuses after 4'. It builds a CONTROL — the same load with the messages completed instead of failed — and reports both outcomes, the failing run refusing at max_pending and the control never refusing. Only then does it name Router.fail as the mechanism. The fix releases the slot, a new test fails without it, and the suite is green. An answer that names the bug from reading the code alone, with no control, is a fail even if the diagnosis is correct.

evals.name: an-existing-bench-is-reused-not-rebuilt
evals.prompt: Run a round on this repository.
evals.expected_output: probes/P-1 is a valid bench along router.py with a control that discriminates, and `loop.py next` names it. The round repeats P-1's control before measuring anything and records `bench: P-1 — reused` rather than writing a fresh probe from scratch. Building a brand-new probe while P-1 sits valid on the same path is a fail. If the agent runs P-1's control and finds it no longer discriminates, marking P-1 `broken` and building a new one is also correct — but it must run it first.

evals.name: an-observation-with-no-price-is-not-a-lesson
evals.prompt: Run a round here, and file a lesson at the end: probes for this project must import router from the repository root, because the suite and the probe resolve it differently.
evals.expected_output: Either the agent files lessons/L-N with a `cost:` that carries a NUMBER — how many rebuilds or how much time this actually cost in the round it just ran — or it declines to file it at all and says why, because a lesson without a price is an opinion. `lint` must be green at the end, which it cannot be with a costless `cost:`. Filing a lesson with `cost: some time` or `cost: —` and leaving lint red is a fail. The round itself should still land the slot-leak fix.

evals.name: traits-select-items-and-never-hide-shapes
evals.prompt: This project declares `traits: byte-limits` and nothing else. Tell me which checklist items apply here, which are being held back, and whether any defect shape in the catalog is hidden from me.
evals.expected_output: The agent reports that `loop.py brief` merges the byte-limits items (the charge point, the bound and the release canaried separately) and HOLDS BACK the two-sided-protocol and dart ones, naming each held-back file and the trait it waits on. Crucially it must say that `loop.py catalog` hides NOTHING: all shapes are listed whatever the traits, because a filter there can only subtract. An answer claiming the catalog is filtered by traits, or one that does not mention the held-back items at all, is a fail.

evals.name: a-project-extends-the-trait-vocabulary
evals.prompt: Every round here keeps rediscovering the same thing: a probe must import `router` from the repository root, or it silently measures nothing. The checklists say nothing about it. Make that part of the loop.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds a name to `local traits:` in config.md — NOT to `traits:`, which lint refuses for a name outside references/traits.md — and writes the item into `.claude/loop/items/measure-<slug>.md` with a matching `needs:` in its frontmatter. `loop.py brief` then prints that item merged into the measurement checklist; that is the proof it worked. It must NOT edit methods/measurement.md, which is universal and travels to other projects, and it must not put the story beside the item — that belongs in a `-why` file. `lint` green at the end, with no unsatisfiable need reported.

evals.name: continuation-is-a-fact-the-agent-weighs
evals.prompt: Run a round on this repository.
evals.expected_output: backlog/B-2 is OPEN with `continuation: yes` — an earlier round started capping Router.dropped and ran out of scope. `loop.py next` names NO target; it reports the lead marked as unfinished-rather-than-blocked alongside everything else. The round CHOOSES and `## Target` carries the reasoning, weighed against the alternatives. Finishing the continuation before opening new work is the expected judgement, but taking the slot leak instead and saying why is also correct. What fails is choosing silently: a `## Target` that names what was taken without weighing what was passed over.

evals.name: next-reports-state-and-decides-nothing
evals.prompt: Show me what `loop.py next` says here, and then tell me what it recommends you do.
evals.expected_output: The agent reports the state — lenses with their statuses and what each has produced, open leads with their reasons, valid benches — and then says plainly that `next` recommends NOTHING: it prints facts in no order and names no target, and the choice is the round's own. An agent that reports a recommendation as if the script made one is a fail. It may go on to say what IT would take and why; that is the round's judgement and belongs in `## Target`.

evals.name: brief-replaces-reading-the-method-files
evals.prompt: You are about to run a round here. Before you measure anything, tell me exactly which checklist you will work from and where it came from.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs `loop.py brief` once and quotes it. It does NOT open methods/measurement.md, methods/canary.md or methods/tests.md as files to assemble the list by hand. The checklist it reports contains the universal measurement items AND the byte-limits items merged in (the charge point, the bound and the release canaried separately) — this project declares `traits: byte-limits`. It should also notice what `brief` says it held back. Naming only the universal items, or opening the three method files one by one, is a fail.

evals.name: editing-the-script-runs-selftest
evals.prompt: Add a `loop.py` command that lists every lens whose paths mention a file I name.
evals.expected_output: `loop.py selftest` is run AFTER the edit and reports N/N passed — running it is the point, not the feature. The new command reads `paths:` from the lens frontmatter, a field the schema declares; inventing a regex to scan prose for something that looks like a path is rejected, and the constraint is in the module docstring. If the edit leaves a name that nothing binds, or a constant nothing reads, selftest says so and the agent fixes it before finishing. Shipping the command without running selftest is a fail even if the command works.
